name: Big-five environment ranking layer v1
status: post-outcome exploratory specification; requires untouched validation
purpose: Rank match environments even when teams have not played each other or have little current-season data, while keeping evidence confidence separate from rank.

history.order: Current-season matches first; fill backward with the immediately previous same-league season.
history.promoted_teams: Do not invent or substitute lower-division history. Mark insufficient comparable history.

ranking_method: Within each weekend, percentile-rank the four pre-match components and calculate a 0-100 weighted score. Rank does not use head-to-head results or the target outcome.

confidence_tiers.A: Both teams have at least three current-season matches in the eight-match history.
confidence_tiers.B: Both teams have at least one current-season match, but one or both have fewer than three.
confidence_tiers.C: One or both teams have zero current-season matches; ranking is historical-only.
confidence_tiers.EXCLUDED: Either team lacks at least five comparable matches, or the required home/away shooting histories are unavailable.

candidate_layer: For each ranked fixture, show confirmed home starters with five same-player/same-team starts within 180 days, ranked by average shots. Mark whether at least two of those starts are current-season.
interpretation: Rank and confidence are separate. A high-ranked Tier C match is interesting but not equivalent to a high-confidence selection.
